title: A self-determination referendum for Catalonia
detail: Negotiate a referendum on Catalan self-determination (*autodeterminació*) with international oversight, the EU and the Council of Europe as mediators, citing Venice Commission guidance. The party says it will remain pro-independence.
c: The Constitutional Court holds that a self-determination referendum in one region conflicts with arts. 1.2 and 2 of the Constitution (sovereignty lies with the whole Spanish people); it would need reform under art. 168 first. Neither PSOE nor PP agrees. In our estimate the EU and the Council of Europe will not mediate a domestic constitutional dispute.

s.t: Constitutional Court ruling 42/2014 on the Catalan sovereignty declaration (BOE)

title: A new funding model for Catalonia
detail: Adopt the funding model agreed with the government in January 2026 (*financiació singular*): Catalonia collects all taxes and pays the state a share for its services, under an "ordinality" principle (*ordinalitat*). The programme says it would bring Catalonia an extra €4.7 billion a year.
c: "Catalonia collects all taxes" is in effect the Basque *concierto*, which the Constitution allows only for the historic territories (first additional provision). It needs reform of the regional funding law LOFCA (176 votes) and probably of the Constitution. Other regions and PP are against, and the Constitutional Court could strike it down.

s.t: Ley Orgánica 8/1980 on regional funding, LOFCA (BOE)

title: Write off more than €17.1 billion of Catalan *FLA* debt
detail: Complete ERC's bill to cancel more than €17.1 billion that the Generalitat owes the state's regional liquidity fund (*FLA*), saving about €1.5 billion a year in interest.
c: The bill to write off €83 billion (€17.1 billion for Catalonia) went to parliament in December 2025. It is an organic law (176 votes), and Junts has not promised support. Under a PP government, no.
pos: Catalonia saves on interest and can spend more on services; the Generalitat's debt falls.
neg: Other regions will demand the same, so state debt grows; moral hazard for regions that borrowed more.

s.t: Finance Ministry, 9 Dec 2025: bill to write off €83,252 million of regional debt sent to parliament

title: Hand immigration and asylum powers to Catalonia
detail: Full powers over immigration and asylum for Catalonia (reception, needs assessment, integration); EU return rules applied only with rights guarantees and no automatic deportations; a new asylum law without offshore processing.
c: Immigration is an exclusive state power (art. 149.1.2 of the Constitution). PSOE agreed a delegation under art. 150.2 with Junts, but Congress rejected it on 23 Sep 2025 (173 for, 177 against). Border functions cannot be handed over at all.

s.t: Congress record, 23 Sep 2025: delegation of immigration powers to Catalonia rejected (173 for, 177 against)

title: A Catalan rental law via art. 150.1 of the Constitution
detail: A state law under art. 150.1 of the Constitution giving the Generalitat full power to regulate urban leases (*LAU*). The programme does not specify rent limits.
c: Art. 150.1 allows legislative powers to be handed over, but civil law on leases is a state power (art. 149.1.8); lawyers consider such a transfer contentious.

title: Higher taxes on non-residential use; 21% VAT on tourist lets
detail: Raise VAT and transfer tax (*ITP*) on homes bought for tourist or seasonal use, second homes and empty flats, and lower them for main homes. 21% VAT on tourist lets, including platforms. Deductions for renovation, protected housing and energy efficiency.
c: 21% VAT on tourist lets is realistic (the EU directive does not stand in the way); ITP is regional, so Catalonia can raise it itself.
pos: An incentive to bring homes back into long-term rental.
neg: Higher taxes on tourism; the effect on housing supply is unclear.

s.t: Directive (EU) 2022/542 on VAT rates (BOE copy of the OJEU)

title: Capital gains tax up to 35%; abolish the Beckham law
detail: Raise the top income tax rate on capital gains from 30% to 35%; lower rates on wages up to €35,000; cut VAT on basic food and hygiene; abolish the Beckham law (*Ley Beckham*: six years taxed as a non-resident) and the regime for international remote workers.
c: Matches PSOE (35% above €300,000); realistic with a left-leaning majority.
pos: Lower tax on wages and higher tax on capital: a fairer split.
neg: An incentive to move capital into holding companies and abroad.

title: A Catalan minimum wage of €1,460
detail: Give the Generalitat power to set a regional minimum wage (*SMC*) of €1,460, and raise the state minimum wage (*SMI*) to 60% of the average gross wage under the European Social Charter.
c: Labour law is an exclusive state power (art. 149.1.7 of the Constitution); a regional minimum wage needs a change to the Workers' Statute and would probably be challenged.
